full_judgment: 18. The learned Single Judge also reversed the finding of the lower appellate Court that the preparation of SA Khatian No. 83, Exhibit 8, municipal assessment in 1961-62 are all collusively done in 1960-61 prior to 1965 when enemy property Ordinance came into force. The learned Single Judge held that it was a mere presumption of the lower appellate Court to hold that in order to save the property from being treated as enemy property all these corrections of SA Khatian and municipal Assessment Register were made. The learned Single Judge also reversed the finding of the lower appellate Court with regard to the plaintiff''s kabala Ext. 1(A) dated 22-11-63 executed by defendant No. 4 by holding that there was no recital that defendant No.4 was the real owner and his brother Birendra defendant No. 3 was simply a name lender. The property is being sold by the real owner and this omission is not very material. Rabindra Kumar Dey possessed the property and let it out to tenants and tenants paid rent to Rabindra Kumar Dey and, as such, Rabindra Kumar Dey treated the property as his own property for all practical purposes. Further, in the sale deed dated 22-11-63 there is a clear recital by vendor Rabindra Kumar Dey that he purchased the property with his own money and for his own interest and owning in his own right. This recital also indirectly reflects that the property was in the benami of his brother.
